messages.content: What is the change in entropy in Joules per Kelvin of a 1kg ice block at 0°C if it is heated to 100°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure?

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

pressure.description: The pressure the substance is under in atmospheres.

message.content:
**Answer:**  
≈ 2.5 kJ K⁻¹ (≈ 2 530 J K⁻¹)

---

### How the number is obtained

| Step | Process | Formula | Value |
|------|---------|---------|-------|
| 1 | **Melting** (ice → water at 0 °C) | ΔS₁ = \(m\,L_f/T_m\) | \(1\,\text{kg}\times 334\,000\ \text{J kg}^{-1}/273.15\ \text{K}=1 222\ \text{J K}^{-1}\) |
| 2 | **Heating water** (0 °C → 100 °C) | ΔS₂ = \(m\,c_{\text{water}}\ln(T_f/T_i)\) | \(1\,\text{kg}\times 4 180\ \text{J kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\times\ln(373.15/273.15)=1 305\ \text{J K}^{-1}\) |

Total entropy change  
\[
\Delta S = \Delta S_1 + \Delta S_2 \approx 1\,222 + 1\,305 = 2\,527\ \text{J K}^{-1}\;\approx\;2.5\ \text{kJ K}^{-1}.
\]

---

### Why vaporisation isn’t included

At 1 atm, water boils at 100 °C. The problem states the block is “heated to 100 °C,” which means the temperature of the material reaches 100 °C. It does **not** require that the entire block has turned into steam; it can simply be liquid water at 100 °C. Therefore, the entropy change stops after the water has been heated to 100 °C. If the question had asked for the entropy change to convert the whole block into steam at 100 °C, an additional term for the latent heat of vaporisation would be added.

The question says "ice block at 0°C if it is heated to 100°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure". That implies the ice melts, then water heats, then water boils to steam at 100°C. So we need to compute ΔS = ΔS_melt + ΔS_heat_water + ΔS_vaporization. Use standard values: latent heat of fusion L_f = 334 kJ/kg, latent heat of vaporization L_v = 2260 kJ/kg. Specific heat capacities: c_ice ~ 2.09 kJ/(kg·K), c_water ~ 4.18 kJ/(kg·K). For steam at 100°C, specific heat capacity of water vapor ~ 2.01 kJ/(kg·K). L_f = 334 kJ/kg = 334000 J/kg. Tm=273.15 K. So ΔS_fusion = 334000 / 273.15 = approx 1222.5 J/K.
